questions.text: In Chekhov's play 'The Proposal', what triggers the first heated argument between Lomov and Natalya, even before he can propose?
options: A disagreement over who owns the Oxen Meadows
A disagreement over Natalya's dowry amount
A disagreement over the wedding date
A disagreement over which school their children should attend
questions.explanation: The two quarrel over ownership of the Oxen Meadows, and later over whose dog is better, before Lomov can even make his proposal — the play's central comic device.

questions.text: In 'A Letter to God', why does Lencho write directly to God?
options: To ask for forgiveness for his sins
To request a hundred pesos so he can resow his hail-destroyed crop
To thank God for a good harvest
questions.explanation: A hailstorm destroys Lencho's entire crop, so he writes to God asking for a hundred pesos to sow his field again before his family starves.

questions.text: What name does Anne Frank give her diary in 'From the Diary of Anne Frank'?
questions.explanation: Anne addresses her diary entries to an imaginary confidante she names 'Kitty', treating the diary almost like a personal friend.
questions.topic: From the Diary of Anne Frank

questions.text: In 'Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom', what does Mandela describe as the 'twin obligations' every person owes?
options: Obligations to one's family and to one's community or country
Obligations to one's employer and to the government
Obligations to education and to religion
Obligations to sport and to art
questions.explanation: Mandela speaks of a man's obligations to his family, parents, wife and children on one hand, and to his people, community and country on the other.
questions.topic: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

questions.text: In 'The Sermon at Benares', what does the Buddha ask Kisa Gotami to fetch in order to 'cure' her dead son?
options: A lamp lit with pure oil
A mustard seed from a house where no one has ever died
A flower that blooms only once a year
questions.explanation: The Buddha sends her to find a mustard seed from a home untouched by death; her failure to find one teaches her that death is universal to all.

questions.text: In 'The Hundred Dresses – I', what does Wanda Petronski repeatedly claim to have at home?
options: A hundred dresses hanging in her closet
questions.explanation: Wanda claims to own a hundred dresses, a claim the other girls mock, not realising she actually owns only one faded blue dress.

questions.text: Which of these places is NOT one of the three regions covered in 'Glimpses of India'?
questions.explanation: 'Glimpses of India' consists of three sections — a baker from Goa, Coorg, and tea from Assam. Kashmir is not covered in the chapter.

questions.text: In 'Madam Rides the Bus', how does Valliamma react when an old woman on the bus warns her about the dangers of the river crossing?
options: She ignores the woman completely and falls asleep
She listens politely, but her resolve to complete the solo trip stays firm
She gets frightened and abandons her plan to ride the bus
She asks an adult passenger to accompany her instead
questions.explanation: Valliamma hears the old woman's cautionary story about the river, but her determination to complete her first solo bus ride is not shaken.

quiz_title: Footprints Without Feet — Quick Revision Quiz

questions.text: In 'Bholi', what was the protagonist's real name, with 'Bholi' being her nickname?
questions.explanation: Sulekha is nicknamed 'Bholi' (the simpleton) by her family because of her pockmarked face and her shyness/stammer as a child.

questions.text: In Maupassant's 'The Necklace', what does Matilda finally discover about the necklace she borrowed and lost?
options: It had been stolen before she borrowed it
It was actually made of paste and worth far less than what she paid to replace it
It belonged to her own family originally
It was never actually lost at all
questions.explanation: After ten years of hard labour to repay the replacement necklace, Matilda learns the original was an imitation worth only a fraction of what she paid.

questions.text: In 'A Triumph of Surgery', why does Tricki the dog fall ill?
options: He is overfed and pampered, leading to obesity and lethargy
He is injured in an accident
He refuses to eat anything at all
questions.explanation: Tricki's owner overfeeds and spoils him with treats, so Mr Herriot puts him on a strict diet and exercise regime to restore his health.

questions.text: In 'The Midnight Visitor', how does Ausable outwit the spy Max and get hold of his gun?
options: He invents a story about a balcony and police waiting outside, prompting Max to look out the window
He overpowers Max in a physical struggle
He calls the police directly in front of Max
He bribes Max with money to leave quietly
questions.explanation: Ausable calmly invents a tale about a balcony and police surveillance, making Max go to the window to check, which lets Ausable seize control of the situation.

questions.text: In 'The Thief's Story', what ultimately makes Hari Singh decide to return Anil's money instead of running away with it?
options: He is caught red-handed by the police
Anil's genuine trust in him, despite being robbed, touches him and changes his resolve
He realises the money is counterfeit
Anil offers him a much larger reward
questions.explanation: Anil's unexpected trust and lack of suspicion toward Hari Singh moves him, and he chooses to return the stolen money rather than flee with it.

questions.text: In 'The Hack Driver', who turns out to be the friendly hack driver who drives the narrator around town?
options: A hired local taxi driver with no connection to the case
Oliver Lutkins himself, the very man the narrator was sent to find
The narrator's own law firm colleague
questions.explanation: The talkative hack driver is revealed to be Oliver Lutkins in disguise, the man the young lawyer had travelled to serve a summons on.

questions.text: In 'The Book That Saved the Earth', which Earth book do the invading Martians mistakenly believe is a dangerous secret weapon?
options: A book of Mother Goose nursery rhymes
questions.explanation: The Martian Think-Tank badly misinterprets a simple book of Mother Goose rhymes as an encoded Earth super-weapon, which leads to the invasion's comic failure.
questions.topic: The Book That Saved the Earth

questions.text: In 'A Question of Trust', why is Horace Danby eventually arrested, even though his safe-cracking that night went almost unnoticed?
options: He is arrested for an earlier, unrelated robbery because he unknowingly left fingerprints after the woman took his gloves
He confesses to the police out of guilt
The homeowner identifies him by his voice
He is caught still inside the house by a security guard
questions.explanation: The mysterious woman takes Horace's gloves, so he leaves fingerprints without realising it; those prints later match an earlier, unrelated robbery and lead to his arrest.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly follows subject-verb agreement?
options: Neither of the boys were present at the meeting.
Neither of the boys was present at the meeting.
Neither of the boys are present at the meeting.
Neither of the boys being present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is treated as singular, so it takes the singular verb 'was', regardless of the plural noun phrase that follows it.

questions.text: Choose the correct article to fill the blank: 'She has ___ interesting idea for the project.'
questions.explanation: 'Interesting' begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article 'an' is used rather than 'a'.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive voice form of: 'The teacher is checking the answer sheets.'
options: The answer sheets are checked by the teacher.
The answer sheets were being checked by the teacher.
The answer sheets are being checked by the teacher.
The answer sheets have been checked by the teacher.
questions.explanation: The present continuous active ('is checking') converts to present continuous passive: 'is/are being + past participle'.

questions.text: In a formal job application letter, which closing phrase is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Formal letters and applications conventionally close with 'Yours sincerely' or 'Yours faithfully', not casual expressions.

questions.text: Before attempting the questions on an unseen comprehension passage, what should a student do first?
options: Guess the answers based on the title alone
Read the passage carefully at least once to understand its overall meaning
Skip straight to writing answers without reading
Memorise the passage word for word
questions.explanation: A careful first reading for overall meaning helps a student locate and frame accurate answers, rather than guessing or memorising.

questions.text: A personal diary entry conventionally begins with which element?
options: A formal salutation such as 'Dear Sir'
The date (and sometimes the day or time) at the top
questions.explanation: Since a diary entry is a personal record of a specific day, it conventionally opens with the date at the top.

questions.text: Choose the sentence with the correctly used article.
options: He is an honest man because he never lies.
He is a honest man because he never lies.
He is an honesty man because he never lies.
He is the honest man because he never lies.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a silent 'h', so the word is pronounced starting with a vowel sound, requiring 'an' rather than 'a'.

questions.text: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I will finish the work tomorrow.'
options: She said that she will finish the work tomorrow.
She said that she would finish the work the next day.
She said that she would finish the work tomorrow.
She says that she would finish the work the next day.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts to 'would' and the time expression 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day' because the reporting verb is in the past tense.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द संधि से बना है?
questions.explanation: 'विद्यालय' विद्या + आलय के मेल से बना है, जहाँ आ + आ = आ होने के कारण यह दीर्घ स्वर संधि का उदाहरण है।

questions.text: 'नदी' शब्द का लिंग पहचानिए।
questions.explanation: हिंदी व्याकरण में 'नदी' सदैव स्त्रीलिंग शब्द माना जाता है।

questions.text: 'मैंने पत्र लिखा।' इस वाक्य में क्रिया किस काल को दर्शाती है?
questions.explanation: 'लिखा' क्रिया-रूप भूतकाल को दर्शाता है, क्योंकि कार्य पहले ही पूर्ण हो चुका है।

questions.text: 'राम ने रावण को मारा' का कर्मवाच्य रूप क्या होगा?
questions.explanation: कर्मवाच्य में कर्म (रावण) वाक्य का विषय बनता है और कर्ता के साथ 'द्वारा' जुड़ता है, इसलिए सही रूप है 'रावण राम द्वारा मारा गया।'

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से द्वंद्व समास का उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: द्वंद्व समास में दोनों पद प्रधान होते हैं और बीच में 'और' का लुप्त भाव रहता है, जैसे 'माता और पिता' = 'माता-पिता'।

questions.text: 'राम ने पुस्तक पढ़ी' वाक्य में 'ने' किस कारक का चिन्ह है?
questions.explanation: 'ने' कर्ता कारक की विभक्ति है, जो यह बताती है कि वाक्य में कार्य करने वाला (राम) कौन है।

questions.text: मुहावरा 'आँखों में धूल झोंकना' का सही अर्थ क्या है?
questions.explanation: इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है छल या धोखे से किसी को वास्तविकता से अनजान रखना।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से व्यंजन संधि का उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: 'सत्+जन' में त् का ज् में परिवर्तन होकर 'सज्जन' बनता है, जो व्यंजन संधि का उदाहरण है; शेष सभी विकल्प स्वर संधि के उदाहरण हैं।

questions.text: 'सूर्य' का सही पर्यायवाची शब्द चुनिए।
questions.explanation: 'दिनकर' सूर्य का ही एक पर्यायवाची शब्द है; शेष विकल्प क्रमशः रात्रि, नदी और आकाश के पर्यायवाची हैं।

questions.text: 'सुख' शब्द का विलोम शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: 'सुख' का सीधा विपरीतार्थक (विलोम) शब्द 'दुःख' है; शेष विकल्प सुख के ही पर्यायवाची हैं।

questions.text: 'कमल के समान नेत्र' पंक्ति में किस अलंकार का प्रयोग हुआ है?
questions.explanation: जहाँ उपमेय (नेत्र) की तुलना उपमान (कमल) से 'समान' जैसे शब्द का प्रयोग करके की जाती है, वहाँ उपमा अलंकार होता है।

questions.text: 'गंगा की गोद में गुनगुनाती गौरैया' पंक्ति में किस अलंकार के दर्शन होते हैं?
questions.explanation: एक ही वर्ण 'ग' की बार-बार आवृत्ति होने के कारण यहाँ अनुप्रास अलंकार है।

questions.text: करुण रस की उत्पत्ति किस स्थायी भाव से होती है?
questions.explanation: करुण रस का स्थायी भाव 'शोक' है, जो प्रियजन के वियोग या दुख की स्थिति में उत्पन्न होता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: 'लड़की' स्त्रीलिंग कर्ता है, इसलिए क्रिया भी स्त्रीलिंग रूप 'पढ़ रही है' में होनी चाहिए।

questions.text: मुहावरा 'हाथ-पैर फूलना' का सही अर्थ है
options: घबरा जाना या भयभीत हो जाना
questions.explanation: इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है किसी स्थिति को देखकर अत्यधिक घबरा जाना या भयभीत हो जाना।

questions.text: दोहा छंद के विषम (प्रथम व तृतीय) चरण में सामान्यतः कितनी मात्राएँ होती हैं?
questions.explanation: दोहा छंद के विषम चरण (पहले व तीसरे) में 13 मात्राएँ और सम चरण (दूसरे व चौथे) में 11 मात्राएँ होती हैं।

questions.text: 'सुंदर' शब्द किस शब्द-भेद के अंतर्गत आता है?
questions.explanation: 'सुंदर' किसी संज्ञा की विशेषता (गुण) बताता है, इसलिए यह विशेषण (adjective) है।

questions.text: 'पुस्तकें' शब्द का एकवचन रूप क्या होगा?
questions.explanation: 'पुस्तकें' बहुवचन रूप है, जिसका एकवचन रूप 'पुस्तक' होता है।

questions.text: प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य के अंत में सामान्यतः कौन-सा विराम चिह्न लगाया जाता है?
questions.explanation: जिस वाक्य में प्रश्न पूछा जाए, उसके अंत में प्रश्नवाचक चिह्न (?) लगाया जाता है।

questions.text: 'सफलता' शब्द में मूल शब्द और प्रत्यय को सही-सही अलग कीजिए।
questions.explanation: मूल शब्द 'सफल' में 'ता' प्रत्यय जोड़कर भाववाचक संज्ञा 'सफलता' बनाई गई है।

questions.text: 'अन्याय' शब्द में प्रयुक्त उपसर्ग पहचानिए।
questions.explanation: 'अन्याय' शब्द 'अन्' उपसर्ग और 'न्याय' मूल शब्द के मेल से बना है, जो निषेध (नकारात्मक) भाव दर्शाता है।

questions.text: 'गंगा-यमुना' शब्द-युग्म किस समास का उदाहरण है?
questions.explanation: दोनों पद (गंगा और यमुना) समान रूप से प्रधान हैं और बीच में 'और' का भाव छिपा है, इसलिए यह द्वंद्व समास है।

questions.text: मुहावरा 'नौ दो ग्यारह होना' का अर्थ है
options: भाग जाना या गायब हो जाना
questions.explanation: इस मुहावरे का अर्थ है अचानक और चुपचाप वहाँ से भाग जाना या गायब हो जाना।

questions.text: 'यहाँ पर बालक और बालिकाएँ खेल रही हैं' वाक्य में त्रुटि है। इसका शुद्ध रूप कौन-सा है?
options: यहाँ पर बालक और बालिकाएँ खेल रहे हैं।
यहाँ पर बालक और बालिकाएँ खेल रही है।
यहाँ पर बालक और बालिकाएँ खेलती है।
यहाँ पर बालक और बालिकाएँ खेल रहा है।
questions.explanation: पुल्लिंग (बालक) और स्त्रीलिंग (बालिकाएँ) दोनों कर्ता एक साथ होने पर क्रिया पुल्लिंग बहुवचन रूप 'खेल रहे हैं' में होनी चाहिए।

questions.text: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, every composite number can be expressed as:
options: A sum of prime numbers in exactly one way
A product of prime numbers, uniquely up to the order of the factors
A product of exactly two primes only
A power of a single prime, always
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states every composite number factorises into primes, and this factorisation is unique apart from the order of the factors.

questions.text: If the zeroes of a quadratic polynomial are 2 and 3, which polynomial (with leading coefficient 1) has these zeroes?
questions.explanation: Sum of zeroes = 2 + 3 = 5 and product of zeroes = 2 × 3 = 6, so the polynomial is x^2 - (sum)x + (product) = x^2 - 5x + 6.

questions.text: For the pair of linear equations a1x + b1y = c1 and a2x + b2y = c2 to have a unique solution, which condition must hold?
questions.explanation: A unique solution exists when the two lines intersect at exactly one point, which happens precisely when a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2.
questions.topic: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

questions.text: What are the roots of the quadratic equation x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factorising gives (x - 3)(x - 4) = 0, so x = 3 and x = 4 are the roots. Check: 3 + 4 = 7 and 3 × 4 = 12, matching the equation.

questions.text: In an Arithmetic Progression with first term 5 and common difference 3, what is the 10th term?
If sin θ = 3/5 for an acute angle θ, what is cos θ?
questions.explanation: Taking opposite = 3 and hypotenuse = 5 in a right triangle, the adjacent side is √(5²-3²) = 4, so cos θ = 4/5.

questions.text: What is the distance between the points (2, 3) and (5, 7)?
questions.explanation: Using the distance formula: √[(5-2)² + (7-3)²] = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.

questions.text: A bag contains 4 red balls and 6 blue balls. What is the probability of drawing a red ball at random?
questions.explanation: There are 4 favourable outcomes out of 10 total balls, so the probability is 4/10, which simplifies to 2/5.

questions.text: When a magnesium ribbon burns in air to form magnesium oxide, which type of chemical reaction occurs?
questions.explanation: Magnesium and oxygen (two reactants) combine to form a single product, magnesium oxide, which is the defining feature of a combination reaction.

questions.text: Which of the following turns red litmus paper blue?
questions.explanation: Bases turn red litmus paper blue, while acids turn blue litmus paper red; neutral substances cause no colour change.

questions.text: Which property is generally true of metals but NOT of non-metals?
options: They are good conductors of heat and electricity
They are brittle in the solid state
They readily gain electrons to form negative ions
questions.explanation: Metals are typically good conductors of heat and electricity due to free-moving electrons, unlike most non-metals which are poor conductors.

questions.text: During human respiration, where does the actual exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between air and blood take place?
questions.explanation: The thin-walled, richly blood-vessel-supplied alveoli are the site of gas exchange between inhaled air and the bloodstream.

questions.text: If the length of a conductor is doubled while its cross-sectional area stays the same, what happens to its resistance?
options: It becomes four times as much
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length (R = ρL/A), so doubling the length while keeping area constant doubles the resistance.

questions.text: Which plant hormone is primarily responsible for phototropism, the bending of a shoot toward light?
questions.explanation: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side of the shoot, promoting faster cell elongation there and causing the shoot to bend toward the light.

questions.text: A concave mirror forms a real, inverted and highly diminished image at its focus when the object is placed:
options: Between the pole and the focus
questions.explanation: When the object is at infinity, parallel rays from it converge at the focus of a concave mirror, forming a real, inverted and highly diminished image there.

questions.text: Using the right-hand thumb rule for a straight current-carrying conductor, what does the curling of the fingers represent, when the thumb points along the current's direction?
options: The direction of the magnetic field lines circling the conductor
The direction of the electric field
The direction of current flow itself
The direction of induced EMF only
questions.explanation: The right-hand thumb rule shows that if the thumb points along the current, the curled fingers indicate the direction of the circular magnetic field around the conductor.

questions.text: What is the primary function of a political party in a democracy?
options: To contest elections and form a government to implement policies
To appoint judges to the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Political parties exist mainly to contest elections, represent voters' interests, and form or oppose the government to shape public policy.

questions.text: In a federal system of government, power is divided between:
options: The central government and the state or provincial governments
The judiciary and the legislature only
questions.explanation: Federalism is a system of government where power is constitutionally divided between a central authority and various constituent state/provincial units.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of horizontal power-sharing?
options: Power shared among the legislature, executive and judiciary at the same level
Power shared between the union government and state governments
Reservation of seats for women in local bodies
Power shared only between community-based organisations
questions.explanation: Horizontal power-sharing distributes power among different organs of government at the same level — legislature, executive and judiciary — so that no single organ becomes too powerful.

questions.text: Which statement best distinguishes 'overlapping' social differences from 'cross-cutting' social differences?
options: Overlapping differences reinforce each other along one dividing line, while cross-cutting differences cut across groups and tend to reduce conflict intensity
Overlapping differences occur only in rural areas
Cross-cutting differences exist only between two political parties
There is no real distinction between the two
questions.explanation: When disadvantages pile up along the same line (overlapping), conflict tends to be sharper; when group memberships cut across each other (cross-cutting), conflict tends to be milder.

questions.text: Which constitutional guarantee allows religious communities in India to set up their own educational institutions?
options: Freedom of religion provisions in the Constitution
questions.explanation: The Indian Constitution's provisions on freedom of religion allow religious communities to establish and administer their own educational institutions.

questions.text: Which of the following is generally considered a genuine strength of democratic government compared to non-democratic alternatives?
options: It guarantees every decision will be economically efficient
It promotes accountability and a legitimate government based on people's consent
It eliminates all forms of inequality instantly
It guarantees rapid economic growth every year
questions.explanation: Democracies are valued less for guaranteeing specific outcomes and more for being accountable, responsive, and legitimate because they rest on the people's consent.

questions.text: Which of these best describes a 'foundational' challenge to democracy, as distinct from an 'expansion' challenge?
options: Transforming a non-democratic regime into a democratic one and setting up basic democratic institutions
Extending democratic principles to more institutions and social groups within an already democratic country
Deepening democracy where it already exists through greater citizen participation
Improving the day-to-day functioning of existing democratic institutions only
questions.explanation: A foundational challenge involves bringing down a non-democratic regime and establishing the basic structures of democracy, unlike expansion or deepening challenges faced within established democracies.

questions.text: The April 2006 movement in Nepal that restored democracy is a textbook example of what kind of political mobilisation?
options: A popular struggle combining political organisations, movement groups and spontaneous public mobilisation
A struggle led purely by the army to seize power
An economic trade dispute between two countries
A judicial reform initiated entirely by the courts
questions.explanation: The April 2006 movement combined political parties, civil society groups and ordinary citizens mobilising together, making it a classic popular struggle for democracy.

questions.text: Resources that can be renewed or replenished naturally within a relatively short time are called:
questions.explanation: Renewable resources, such as solar energy or forests, can regenerate or be replenished naturally within a relatively short span of time.

questions.text: Which of the following is a kharif crop, sown with the onset of the monsoon in India?
questions.explanation: Rice is a typical kharif crop, sown in the rainy season (June-July) and harvested around September-October; wheat, mustard and gram are rabi crops.

questions.text: Which of the following is a traditional method of rainwater harvesting practised in many parts of India?
options: Rooftop rainwater harvesting into storage tanks
questions.explanation: Rooftop rainwater harvesting, where rain is collected and stored in tanks or channelled to recharge groundwater, is a long-practised traditional method in India.

questions.text: Which of these is classified as a non-conventional (renewable) source of energy?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is a non-conventional, renewable energy source, unlike coal, petroleum and natural gas, which are conventional, exhaustible fossil fuels.

questions.text: Based on the source of its raw material, which category does the iron and steel industry belong to?
questions.explanation: The iron and steel industry draws its main raw material, iron ore, from minerals, so it is classified as a mineral-based industry.

questions.text: Species whose population has declined so much that they are at risk of extinction are classified as:
questions.explanation: Endangered species are those whose numbers have fallen to a level that puts them at risk of extinction if the decline continues.

questions.text: Which mode of transport in India carries the bulk of long-distance, heavy and bulky freight at relatively low cost?
questions.explanation: Railways are the backbone of India's inland transport system for moving heavy and bulky goods cheaply over long distances.

questions.text: Land that remains uncultivated for one or more agricultural years but less than five years, to let it regain fertility, is classified as:
questions.explanation: Fallow land is cultivable land left temporarily unused (under five years) to restore fertility, unlike wasteland, which is unfit for cultivation.

questions.text: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in which year?
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Gandhi in 1920, urging Indians to withdraw cooperation from British institutions.

questions.text: In the years following the French Revolution, French artists and poets personified the 'nation' as a woman, giving her the name:
questions.explanation: French revolutionaries personified Liberty and the Nation as a female figure named Marianne, whose image became a symbol of republican France.
questions.topic: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

questions.text: Which mid-fifteenth-century invention dramatically increased the speed and scale of book production in Europe?
questions.explanation: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, developed around the mid-1400s, allowed books to be produced far faster and more cheaply than by hand-copying.
questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World

questions.text: In pre-industrial Europe, what term describes the system where merchants supplied raw materials to rural households, who produced goods from their own homes for a wider market?
questions.explanation: Before factories became dominant, merchants used the putting-out system (proto-industrialisation), supplying raw material to rural producers who worked from home.

questions.text: The mass migration of indentured labourers from India in the nineteenth century was primarily to work on:
options: Plantations in colonies such as the Caribbean, Mauritius and Fiji
questions.explanation: Thousands of Indian indentured labourers were shipped to work on sugar, tea and rubber plantations in colonies like the Caribbean islands, Mauritius and Fiji.
questions.topic: The Making of a Global World

questions.text: The Simon Commission of 1928 was widely opposed by Indians chiefly because:
options: It did not include a single Indian member
It proposed complete independence too quickly
It was formed by the Indian National Congress itself
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission was boycotted because it was composed entirely of British members with no Indian representation, which many saw as insulting.

questions.text: In colonial India, why did many handloom weavers face a sharp decline in demand for their cloth during the nineteenth century?
options: Cheap machine-made cloth imported from British mills flooded Indian markets
The colonial government banned handloom weaving entirely
Cotton cultivation stopped completely in India
Weavers voluntarily shifted to farming en masse
questions.explanation: Machine-made cloth from British mills was cheaper and flooded Indian markets, undercutting demand for hand-woven cloth and devastating many weaving communities.

questions.text: How did the spread of print culture contribute to the rise of nationalism in colonial India?
options: It had no real connection to nationalist politics
It allowed ideas, news and nationalist arguments to circulate widely through newspapers, pamphlets and books, building shared public opinion
It was used exclusively by the colonial government for administration
It only helped spread religious texts with no political content
questions.explanation: Newspapers, pamphlets and books let nationalist ideas reach a wide, dispersed readership, helping build shared political consciousness across regions.
questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World

questions.text: Which of these is commonly used, alongside other indicators, as a measure of a country's development by comparing average income?
questions.explanation: Per capita income (average income per person) is a commonly used comparative measure of development, though it is not the only indicator used.

questions.text: Activities such as farming, fishing and mining that directly exploit natural resources belong to which sector of the economy?
questions.explanation: The primary sector covers activities that directly use natural resources, such as agriculture, fishing, forestry and mining.

questions.text: Which institution is the apex body that regulates and supervises the banking system in India?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank that regulates and supervises all banks and the overall banking system in the country.

questions.text: Under India's consumer protection system, which forum would a consumer typically approach first for a grievance of relatively small monetary value?
options: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum/Commission
The Supreme Court of India directly
questions.explanation: India's three-tier consumer dispute redressal system begins at the district level for cases up to a certain value, before escalating to state and national commissions.

questions.text: What does 'globalisation' primarily refer to in an economic context?
options: The closer integration of countries through trade, investment, and the flow of capital, labour and services
A single country becoming fully self-reliant and stopping all trade
A policy restricting all foreign companies from operating locally
The conversion of all national currencies into one global currency
questions.explanation: Globalisation refers to the growing interconnection of economies through trade, investment, capital flows and movement of people and services across borders.

questions.text: When the value of goods and services produced by a sector is divided by the number of people employed in it, what does this measure represent?
options: Productivity, or output per worker, in that sector
The total GDP of the whole country
The literacy rate of the sector's workers
questions.explanation: Dividing a sector's total output value by the number of workers in it gives a measure of productivity, or output per worker.

questions.text: Why might formal sources of credit, like banks, generally be preferred by borrowers over informal sources, like moneylenders?
options: Formal credit is typically regulated by the RBI and charges lower, more transparent interest rates
Formal credit requires absolutely no documentation
Informal lenders are legally required to charge the same rate as banks
questions.explanation: Formal sources are regulated by the RBI and generally offer lower, transparent interest rates, while informal lenders can charge very high rates with little oversight.

questions.text: Why do economists argue that an average measure like per capita income can sometimes hide important facts about real development?
options: Because an average can mask large income inequalities between the richest and poorest in a population
Because per capita income is always calculated incorrectly
Because averages apply only to agricultural economies
Because per capita income automatically decreases every year
questions.explanation: An average figure does not show how income is actually distributed, so two regions with the same per capita income can still have very different levels of real inequality.
